subject.title: Google Chat: Add user OAuth support for reactions and media uploads

question: Should privileged Google Chat operations use consent-based OAuth refresh tokens or Workspace domain-wide delegation, and what minimum scopes and operator controls are acceptable?
rationale: The capability gap is established, but the two viable user-auth models have materially different administrator, consent, impersonation, secret-storage, revocation, and blast-radius implications that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Domain-wide delegation
options.body: Use the existing service-account credential with a required impersonated user subject and narrowly configured Google Chat scopes as an explicit administrator-controlled mode.

options.title: Refresh-token OAuth
options.body: Add OAuth client and refresh-token SecretRefs with a documented authorization, refresh, rotation, and revocation workflow.

options.title: Keep app authentication only
options.body: Decline user credentials and instead improve unsupported-operation warnings and app-auth media fallbacks.

recommendation.title: Domain-wide delegation
recommendation.body: Use the existing service-account credential with a required impersonated user subject and narrowly configured Google Chat scopes as an explicit administrator-controlled mode.
